subdomain: 3.4 Analyze observability challenges and select monitoring strategies at scale

en.question: A Claude Messages API 2026-10-21 service uses server-sent events. Its dashboard records success when HTTP 200 arrives, but some streams later emit an overload error and never deliver a complete answer. Which monitoring change best exposes this reliability gap?

options.text: Record the first content event as success instead of recording the HTTP response status.
options.note: An early content event still precedes possible stream errors or incomplete generation. Moving the success marker slightly later does not establish a completed answer.

options.text: Count a request as successful whenever at least one output token is reported in usage.
options.note: A failed stream can generate billable tokens before interruption. Token production is not evidence that the user received a complete acceptable response.

options.text: Exclude streaming requests from error-rate monitoring and compare only their time to first token.
options.note: Time to first token measures responsiveness, not stream reliability. Excluding these requests hides the failures rather than accounting for their terminal state.

options.text: Track stream error events, normal completion, final stop reason, and application outcome with the provider request ID.
options.note: Streaming errors can occur after HTTP status is committed. Terminal stream state and application outcome distinguish a delivered answer from an interrupted attempt, while the request ID supports investigation.
